  "USA_1970_NIX_V0": "The Vietnam review must confront American commitments, allied readiness and the political cost of continued war. Operational choices require a common assessment rather than separate promises to commanders, Congress and the public.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V1": "An operational ceiling places defined limits on the war effort. It can reduce uncertainty and administrative strain while restricting the freedom commanders claim they need to achieve their objectives.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V2": "Vietnamization with conditions would tie the transfer of responsibility to the capabilities and decisions of the South Vietnamese government. American support must have practical terms rather than assume that a timetable alone creates readiness.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V3": "Maximum pressure seeks leverage through a greater willingness to use American power. It also exposes the administration to the military, political and financial consequences of an intensified campaign.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V4": "The Paris channel offers a means of testing a negotiated outcome while fighting continues. Keeping it open requires the administration to distinguish useful bargaining from the expectation that diplomacy will simply ratify its preferred terms.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V5": "Supporting the ARVN must address training, equipment and the responsibilities its government is prepared to assume. A request for cooperation needs an accepted agreement before American intentions can become a dependable allied commitment.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V6": "Cross-border operations would widen the geographic reach of American military pressure. Authorising them raises questions about sovereign boundaries, congressional authority and the costs of extending an already difficult war.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V7": "Insisting on terms rather than a timetable preserves bargaining flexibility. The administration must accept the continuing domestic and financial burden of a war whose end is not fixed in advance.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V8": "Congressional operational limits would place part of the war's direction under clearer legislative control. The arrangement can improve constitutional confidence while narrowing presidential and military discretion.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_V9": "Defending commander-in-chief authority keeps operational decisions concentrated in the executive. The White House must weigh that freedom against the distrust and institutional opposition it may intensify.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F0": "The Nixon Doctrine asks partners to carry more of their own defence while America remains a central source of support. Its implementation must distinguish sustainable assistance from obligations Washington can no longer carry indefinitely.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F1": "A secret channel to Beijing offers contact outside the expectations of familiar alignments. Discretion can make exploration possible, but a durable opening will eventually require terms both governments are prepared to defend.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F2": "Linkage seeks to connect strategic restraint with wider conduct between the superpowers. Arms negotiations can become part of that bargain, provided each government sees credible reasons to honour the resulting limits.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F3": "Allies need reassurance that a changing American strategy does not mean abandonment. Maintaining confidence requires concrete cooperation alongside a clearer account of the responsibilities Washington expects partners to assume.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F4": "A presidential visit to Beijing can turn private contact into a visible political opening. Its significance rests on an accepted relationship, while disagreements and the concerns of existing partners remain part of the diplomatic cost.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F5": "A Moscow summit offers the opportunity to place strategic negotiations within a broader relationship. The administration must seek agreements its counterpart will accept without confusing an important meeting with the resolution of every rivalry.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F6": "Okinawa's reversion requires agreement over sovereignty and the practical continuation of security arrangements. Negotiators must reconcile local and Japanese expectations with the American military responsibilities attached to the islands.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F7": "The Jordanian crisis puts regional security and the limits of American influence under pressure. Washington must assess the parties' actual actions before choosing how far its diplomatic and military support should reach.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F8": "Reliance on an Israeli deterrent favours regional military strength as a restraint on hostile action. The administration must consider how that support affects its relationships with other governments and the space for a negotiated settlement.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_F9": "The Rogers approach seeks a diplomatic framework for reducing regional conflict. Reviving it requires proposals the parties can accept, rather than an assumption that American sponsorship alone supplies the missing agreement.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_M0": "The Gates Commission asks whether military manpower can be sustained without the existing draft. Its recommendations must be judged against recruiting, personnel costs and the social obligations attached to national service.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_M1": "An all-volunteer transition would change the relationship between service and citizenship. Better recruitment and professional incentives require a budget capable of attracting and retaining the personnel the armed forces need.",
  "USA_1970_NIX_M2": "Reforming Selective Service would retain conscription while addressing the administration and fairness of the system. The government must defend both its manpower requirements and the obligations it imposes on those selected.",
  "USA_1970_1972_democratic_victory": "A Democratic victory gives the new administration a mandate to challenge the executive practices and economic priorities of its predecessor. Congressional relations and the continuing war will determine how much of that promise can become policy.",
  "USA_1970_1972_republican_victory": "A Republican victory renews the administration's claim to pursue its economic and diplomatic programme. The next term must turn electoral strength into commitments that Congress, state governments and foreign partners are prepared to support.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_1_end_the_imperial_presidency": "Restoring limits on presidential power requires institutions capable of enforcing them. The new administration will give Congress a stronger place in decisions that previous executives treated as matters of unilateral national necessity.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_2_jobs_before_fine_tuning": "Employment will take priority over confidence in adjustments that have not reached struggling communities. Federal support can bring activity forward, while leaving the government responsible for the cost and inflationary risks of intervention.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_3_congressional_review_of_the_vietnam_war": "Congressional review would put the purposes and conduct of the Vietnam commitment before the legislature. Public scrutiny can strengthen constitutional authority while restricting operational freedom claimed by the executive.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_4_war_powers_and_conversion": "War-powers reform and industrial conversion connect constitutional limits to the economy sustained by military commitments. The administration must provide a practical transition for workers and enterprises affected by a change in national priorities.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_5_emergency_employment_act": "Emergency employment measures can reach communities where recovery has left too many workers behind. Projects must provide useful work and public value rather than make their continuation an end in itself.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_6_the_case_church_amendment": "A legislative limit on military operations gives Congress a concrete instrument for ending commitments it will no longer finance. The choice changes the executive's room for manoeuvre and places greater responsibility on the public terms of policy.",
  "USA_1970_1972_dem_7_congressional_budget_and_impoundment_control_act": "Budget control must define the relationship between appropriations and executive discretion. Clearer congressional procedures can strengthen accountability while making fiscal decisions depend on a more demanding legislative bargain.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_1_a_strategy_of_leverage_in_vietnam": "A strategy of leverage seeks to improve negotiating terms through sustained pressure and allied support. Its advocates must defend the continuing commitments before a Congress and public increasingly attentive to the war's costs.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_2_new_federalism_in_practice": "The next stage of New Federalism will give state and local institutions a larger role in public programmes. Washington must reconcile reduced central direction with responsibility for the uneven capacity of its partners.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_3_d_tente_with_leverage": "Détente with leverage combines negotiation with a continuing claim to strategic strength. The administration must make cooperation credible without asking supporters to regard every compromise as a retreat.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_4_pacific_trade_openings": "Pacific trade offers producers access to growing commercial relationships. The opening must be supported by terms American firms can use and a policy able to address the industries exposed to stronger competition.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_5_state_export_development_grants": "State export grants can connect local producers to markets beyond familiar domestic customers. Professional commercial support will help smaller enterprises participate without turning assistance into a permanent subsidy for established interests.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_6_east_west_trade_negotiations": "East-West trade negotiations seek commercial gains across a strategic divide. The government must balance access and confidence with the security restrictions and political conditions attached to the relationship.",
  "USA_1970_1972_rep_7_the_trade_act_of_1974": "A trade settlement must define how the executive negotiates and how exposed industries are treated. The administration will seek a framework capable of widening commerce while retaining sufficient congressional support.",
  "USA_1970_1972_common_energy_reorganization_act": "Energy responsibilities scattered across agencies make a common strategy harder to sustain. Reorganisation can clarify public authority, provided the new structure addresses practical supply and regulatory problems rather than merely rearranging offices.",
  "USA_1970_1976_democratic_victory": "A Democratic mandate raises expectations of accountable government and a renewed social commitment. Economic uncertainty and energy dependence will test whether confidence in the new administration can be matched by practical results.",
  "USA_1970_1976_republican_victory": "A Republican mandate offers support for restraint and enterprise during a difficult economic period. The administration must decide how to reduce public burdens without leaving recovery dependent on promises alone.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_1_government_as_good_as_its_promise": "Government can recover confidence by meeting clear obligations and exposing decisions to scrutiny. The administration will ask its agencies to demonstrate competence as well as defend the moral purpose of public action.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_2_a_national_energy_effort": "A national energy effort connects household consumption, industry and imported supply. Bringing those interests into one programme requires sustained public investment and a willingness to confront costs that individual consumers cannot solve alone.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_3_economic_stimulus_appropriations_act_of_1977": "Stimulus appropriations can bring work and public investment forward where private demand remains weak. The administration must use the temporary opening to create durable value rather than obligations unsupported by a later revenue base.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_4_create_the_department_of_energy": "A Department of Energy would bring policy and coordination into a stronger common institution. Its authority must be matched by technical competence and cooperation with the agencies and industries it is expected to guide.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_5_employment_and_transport_reform": "Employment and transport policy can reinforce one another when investment connects people to useful work. The government will seek improvements that serve everyday economic activity as well as immediate recovery.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_6_urban_development_action_grants": "Urban development grants can help communities assemble investment that private finance will not undertake alone. Public support must be tied to credible local projects and benefits that extend beyond their developers.",
  "USA_1970_1976_dem_7_humphrey_hawkins_full_employment_act": "A full-employment commitment makes national economic objectives more explicit. Its credibility will depend on the tools and resources Congress is willing to support when price stability and employment pull policy in different directions.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_1_inflation_first": "Inflation-first policy asks households and firms to accept restraint in pursuit of more stable expectations. The government must account for the immediate burden placed on employment and investment while defending the longer-term objective.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_2_unblock_american_enterprise": "Removing obstacles to enterprise can widen investment and reduce the cost of compliance. Reform must distinguish rules that obstruct productive activity from protections whose removal merely shifts costs onto other citizens.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_3_capital_formation_program": "Capital formation requires predictable rules and incentives to invest beyond the next quarter. The programme will favour new productive capacity while accepting less immediate revenue from the enterprises it seeks to encourage.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_4_unlock_domestic_energy": "Domestic energy development can reduce reliance on external supply. The administration must reconcile access and investment with regulatory responsibilities and the local consequences of a wider extraction programme.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_5_a_balanced_budget_compromise": "A balanced-budget compromise requires agreement over real spending and revenue choices. Its political value depends on sharing responsibility rather than making commitments whose costs are deferred beyond the present administration.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_6_accelerated_depreciation_and_investment_credit": "Depreciation rules and investment credits can make modern equipment more attractive to firms. The treasury will forgo revenue now in the expectation that productive renewal creates a stronger economic base later.",
  "USA_1970_1976_rep_7_kemp_roth_growth_program": "The growth programme seeks a broader investment response through lower tax burdens. Its advocates must persuade Congress that the expected gains justify the immediate pressure on federal revenue and the competing demands on the budget.",
  "USA_1970_1976_common_national_energy_act": "A national energy act must connect incentives, conservation and public responsibilities in a framework capable of implementation. Its compromises will shape how the country distributes the cost of reducing energy vulnerability.",
  "USA_1970_1980_democratic_victory": "A renewed Democratic mandate places recovery and the social contract at the centre of government. The administration must demonstrate that public investment can improve productive capacity without losing control of continuing fiscal obligations.",
  "USA_1970_1980_republican_victory": "A Republican mandate gives the administration an opportunity to change taxes, regulation and defence priorities. Translating that programme into government will require choices over the public costs of incentives and renewed strategic commitments.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_1_targeted_recovery_and_full_employment": "Targeted recovery will concentrate support on workers and regions left outside general growth. Employment objectives must be linked to productive opportunities if public intervention is to create more than temporary relief.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_2_modernize_the_social_contract": "Modernising the social contract requires services and protections suited to changing work and family life. The government must improve their practical value while building a revenue base capable of carrying them.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_3_arms_control_with_readiness": "Arms control can reduce danger without abandoning the maintenance of existing forces. Negotiations and readiness must support the same strategy rather than become rival promises made to different constituencies.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_4_the_industrial_modernization_act": "Industrial modernisation will support equipment, skills and methods that firms struggle to finance on their own. Clear standards can help public investment improve competitiveness without simply protecting obsolete production.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_5_a_peace_dividend_for_human_security": "A peace dividend would redirect resources from military priorities towards domestic security in work, health and community life. The government must make that transition credible without neglecting the forces and commitments it retains.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_6_regional_development_banks": "Regional development banks can bring investment decisions closer to local productive needs. Professional lending standards will be essential if broader access is to create viable enterprises rather than another protected political clientele.",
  "USA_1970_1980_dem_7_a_national_industrial_policy": "A national industrial policy seeks coordination between finance, skills and productive investment. Its institutions must learn from actual results and avoid treating every established industry as a permanent national priority.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_1_across_the_board_tax_relief": "Across-the-board relief promises households and firms a larger claim on their income. The administration must defend its expected effect on activity while confronting the immediate revenue sacrificed by the federal government.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_2_roll_back_the_administrative_state": "Reducing the reach of federal administration gives private and state institutions more discretion. The programme must decide which responsibilities can be removed and which costs will simply reappear elsewhere.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_3_rearm_and_reassure": "Rearmament offers allies a more visible American commitment and suppliers a larger flow of orders. Sustaining it requires trained personnel and finances capable of supporting more than the initial procurement programme.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_4_supply_side_investment_zones": "Investment zones will use targeted incentives to attract enterprise into selected places. Their success depends on productive activity that remains useful after the advantages of location and tax treatment have been counted.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_5_restore_the_defense_industrial_base": "The defence industrial base needs suppliers, tooling and skills capable of meeting a sustained programme. Restoring them will strengthen military production while drawing investment towards priorities chosen by the national security state.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_6_the_1981_budget_resolution": "The budget resolution must turn the administration's competing promises into a congressional agreement. Spending, taxes and strategic commitments will reveal where the governing coalition is prepared to bear the cost of its programme.",
  "USA_1970_1980_rep_7_the_economic_recovery_tax_act": "A recovery tax act seeks a lasting change in incentives for income and investment. Its terms must connect the promise of faster growth to a fiscal settlement the government can actually administer.",
  "USA_1970_1980_common_social_security_compromise": "A Social Security compromise must reconcile confidence in promised benefits with the resources required to finance them. An agreement crossing party lines can give the settlement greater durability than a temporary budget victory.",
  "USA_1970_1984_democratic_victory": "A Democratic victory gives the administration a mandate to reconsider military expenditure and the sources of industrial strength. Its programme must join constitutional accountability to a practical response for workers and communities affected by changing priorities.",
  "USA_1970_1984_republican_victory": "A Republican victory renews support for strategic strength and a government more closely aligned with enterprise. The administration must manage the budgetary and institutional demands created by the programme it seeks to extend.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_1_defense_conversion_and_industrial_renewal": "Defence conversion can redirect skills and equipment towards civilian production. Industrial renewal must provide credible opportunities for workers and firms rather than assume that reduced military orders automatically create a new market.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_2_a_verifiable_nuclear_freeze": "A nuclear freeze needs verification sufficient to make restraint acceptable to both sides. The government will seek a negotiated limit while addressing the security concerns of officials and allies asked to support it.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_3_congressional_control_of_covert_wars": "Congressional control would put covert commitments under clearer democratic responsibility. Oversight can constrain abuses while reducing the freedom intelligence officials claim they need to pursue opportunities abroad.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_4_the_industrial_skills_compact": "An industrial skills compact connects education and production to a shared modernisation effort. Public support should widen access to useful training and help firms adopt methods their existing workforce can sustain.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_5_technology_security_under_law": "Technological security requires a relationship between research, commerce and lawful intelligence activity. Clear boundaries can protect valuable capabilities without allowing national security claims to displace every other public responsibility.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_6_technology_extension_partnerships": "Technology extension can bring practical expertise to firms unable to maintain their own large research establishments. Partnerships must translate innovation into usable production methods rather than another layer of promotional administration.",
  "USA_1970_1984_dem_7_omnibus_trade_and_competitiveness_act_of_1988": "Trade and competitiveness legislation must address both outside competition and domestic productive weaknesses. A lasting framework will connect commercial rules to the skills and investment needed by American enterprises.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_1_the_1985_budget_resolution": "The budget resolution must reconcile fiscal restraint with the administration's strategic programme. Congressional agreement will expose which priorities retain protection and where the government expects the burden of adjustment to fall.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_2_a_strategic_defense_shield": "A strategic defence shield promises protection through demanding technological development. The effort can mobilise research and industry, but its cost and strategic implications require a commitment extending far beyond a declaration of ambition.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_3_negotiate_from_strength": "Negotiating from strength seeks to make an arms agreement compatible with continued military credibility. The administration must turn that leverage into terms its counterpart will accept and its own supporters will honour.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_4_the_high_technology_defense_economy": "High-technology defence orders can support specialised research and production. Their wider value depends on a capable supplier base and the management of commitments that can become expensive to change once established.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_5_a_forward_doctrine_with_guardrails": "A forward doctrine requires readiness beyond the continental homeland and clear limits on how that power will be used. Defined responsibilities can make commitments more credible without treating every regional crisis as an unlimited mission.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_6_reform_defense_procurement": "Procurement reform must make the relationship between military requirements and industrial delivery more accountable. Better methods can improve the value of defence spending while challenging established interests within services and suppliers.",
  "USA_1970_1984_rep_7_goldwater_nichols_department_of_defense_reorganization_act": "Defence reorganisation seeks clearer joint responsibilities across service boundaries. Its success depends on authority and professional practice that can overcome rival institutions without losing their specialised competence.",
  "USA_1970_1984_common_immigration_reform_and_control_act": "Immigration reform must reconcile residence, employment and the enforcement of public rules. A durable settlement needs an administration capable of carrying out the bargain rather than leave employers and households in continuing uncertainty.",
  "USA_1970_1988_democratic_victory": "A Democratic mandate comes as strategic and financial conditions are changing. The administration must decide how to use reduced military pressure while addressing the institutions and communities exposed by domestic financial failures.",
  "USA_1970_1988_republican_victory": "A Republican mandate gives the government responsibility for preserving confidence during international change and domestic financial strain. Continuity must be matched by decisions capable of dealing with problems inherited from earlier expansion.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_1_claim_the_peace_dividend": "A peace dividend would turn changing strategic conditions into room for domestic priorities. The government must judge which commitments can be reduced responsibly and how the released resources will serve productive public purposes.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_2_resolve_the_savings_and_loan_crisis": "Resolving savings-and-loan failures requires public authority able to distinguish recoverable institutions from losses that must be recognised. Restoring confidence will impose costs that ordinary depositors and the treasury cannot simply avoid.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_3_convert_arms_to_industry": "Converting military capacity towards civilian industry requires customers, investment and suitable skills. The transition should preserve useful productive capability rather than assume that any military plant can immediately sell to a different market.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_4_financial_institutions_reform_recovery_and_enforcement_act": "Financial reform must address failed institutions and the standards that allowed losses to accumulate. Recovery and enforcement belong together if public intervention is to restore confidence rather than conceal the same weaknesses.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_5_worker_adjustment_assistance": "Workers displaced by changing industrial and defence priorities need a practical route into new employment. Adjustment assistance will be most useful when training and income support connect to opportunities that actually exist.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_6_create_the_resolution_trust_corporation": "A dedicated resolution institution can give the government a clearer mechanism for handling failed financial assets. Its mandate must make losses visible while seeking an orderly recovery of value for the public.",
  "USA_1970_1988_dem_7_the_peace_dividend_budget": "A peace-dividend budget must turn strategic change into actual choices over spending and revenue. The administration must demonstrate how reduced commitments support domestic goals without neglecting the capabilities it still promises to maintain.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_1_a_federal_resolution_of_the_s_l_crisis": "Federal resolution will place the government behind an orderly response to financial failures. Its responsibilities include protecting confidence and recognising the cost of losses rather than leaving weak institutions to expand their claims indefinitely.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_2_steward_a_changing_soviet_order": "A changing Soviet order presents opportunities for reduced tension alongside new uncertainty. American policy must respond to actual developments without assuming that political change has already settled every strategic concern.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_3_fiscal_responsibility_without_surrender": "Fiscal responsibility requires constraints on commitments the government would otherwise prefer to preserve. The administration must build a bargain that recognises those limits while retaining the core of its strategic and domestic programme.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_4_collective_security_limited_aims": "Collective security can share the burden of responding to aggression. Limited aims and accepted commitments will be essential if cooperation is to avoid becoming an open-ended American obligation.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_5_enforce_budget_rules": "Budget rules matter only when inconvenient choices remain subject to them. Enforcing the framework can strengthen confidence, but will require the governing coalition to accept limits on favoured spending and tax commitments.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_6_base_realignment_and_closure": "Realigning and closing bases can adapt the military establishment to changing requirements. The government must address local economic dependence while distinguishing useful infrastructure from capacity retained chiefly through political protection.",
  "USA_1970_1988_rep_7_the_1990_budget_agreement": "A budget agreement must distribute responsibility for the costs of restraint and revenue. A bargain capable of surviving partisan pressure can give fiscal policy greater stability than a succession of temporary fixes.",
  "USA_1970_1988_common_americans_with_disabilities_act": "Equal access for Americans with disabilities requires changes in employment, services and public space. The commitment will be judged by practical participation as well as the legal recognition of rights.",
  "USA_1970_1992_democratic_victory": "A Democratic victory opens a contest over how investment, social opportunity and deficit reduction should fit together. The administration needs a coalition capable of financing its ambitions without treating fiscal responsibility as someone else's task.",
  "USA_1970_1992_republican_victory": "A Republican victory gives the government an opportunity to recast federal obligations and the role of the states. Its mandate must become a workable settlement over budgets, welfare and the responsibilities of public institutions.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_1_a_deficit_reduction_coalition": "Deficit reduction requires a coalition willing to accept concrete revenue and spending choices. The administration must demonstrate that restraint can support confidence without abandoning the productive investments central to its mandate.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_2_an_investment_led_recovery": "An investment-led recovery would place skills, infrastructure and productive opportunity ahead of short-term relief alone. Public commitments must be chosen for returns that can justify their cost beyond the present administration.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_3_pay_as_you_go_budget_rules": "Pay-as-you-go rules ask new commitments to identify their financing. Enforcing that discipline can strengthen fiscal confidence while making every attractive proposal part of a more demanding legislative bargain.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_4_community_investment_and_health_security": "Community investment and health security connect economic opportunity to the stability of ordinary households. The administration must provide institutions and resources capable of delivering those commitments across very different local conditions.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_5_expand_the_earned_income_tax_credit": "An expanded earned-income credit would support lower-paid work through the tax system. Its reach depends on access and administration, while the government accepts a continuing fiscal commitment to the households it intends to assist.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_6_community_health_and_opportunity_grants": "Community grants can give local institutions resources to address health and opportunity together. Clear priorities and accountable delivery will determine whether support reaches households beyond the organisations best equipped to obtain federal funds.",
  "USA_1970_1992_dem_7_omnibus_budget_reconciliation_act_of_1993": "Budget reconciliation can bring revenue and spending changes into a single governing settlement. Its passage will require the coalition to bear the political cost of choices that cannot all be presented as immediate gains.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_1_balance_the_budget_by_statute": "A statutory commitment to balance the budget would constrain later fiscal choices. Its credibility depends on rules Congress and the executive will follow when economic conditions make compliance politically difficult.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_2_responsibility_before_entitlement": "Placing responsibility before entitlement would change the conditions attached to public support. The government must decide how expectations of work and independence relate to households whose opportunities remain limited.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_3_return_power_to_the_states": "Returning power to the states allows more local discretion over public programmes. Washington must accept less uniform provision while defining which national responsibilities remain enforceable.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_4_state_welfare_compacts": "State welfare compacts can exchange flexibility for explicit commitments over support and administration. Their terms must be practical enough to judge performance rather than merely relocate political responsibility.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_5_block_grants_to_the_states": "Block grants replace detailed federal direction with a broader financial allocation. State governments gain discretion while assuming greater responsibility for how limited resources meet continuing needs.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_6_enterprise_zones": "Enterprise zones use place-based incentives to attract investment and work. Their success depends on productive activity and access for local residents rather than the relocation of firms seeking temporary advantages.",
  "USA_1970_1992_rep_7_personal_responsibility_and_work_opportunity_act": "Welfare reform will redefine the relationship between federal support, state administration and individual obligation. The settlement must establish workable rules while acknowledging the consequences for households whose support is being changed.",
  "USA_1970_1992_common_telecommunications_act": "Telecommunications reform must adapt public rules to changing networks and markets. Greater commercial freedom can encourage investment while raising new questions about competition, access and the responsibilities of providers.",
  "USA_1970_1996_democratic_victory": "A renewed Democratic mandate brings fiscal discipline into contact with the opportunities and risks of a more connected economy. The administration must show how technological change and wider commerce can support citizens beyond the most successful sectors.",
  "USA_1970_1996_republican_victory": "A Republican mandate gives the administration an opportunity to combine fiscal reform with a narrower view of federal responsibilities. New technology and changing security requirements will test the practical limits of that programme.",
  "USA_1970_1996_dem_1_lock_in_fiscal_discipline": "Fiscal discipline must survive the temptation to treat every favourable development as permanent room for spending. A stronger framework can give future decisions a clearer basis while limiting the government's immediate freedom to promise new commitments.",
  "USA_1970_1996_dem_2_responsible_globalization": "Wider global commerce creates gains and concentrated adjustment costs. Responsible participation requires domestic institutions able to help workers and communities respond without assuming that aggregate growth settles every local loss.",
  "USA_1970_1996_dem_3_modernize_federal_information_systems": "Federal information systems support services and decisions across the administration. Modernisation must connect new equipment to trained staff and dependable procedures rather than simply replace one generation of incompatible machinery with another.",
  "USA_1970_1996_dem_4_globalization_adjustment_and_digital_classrooms": "Adjustment support and digital classrooms can widen access to a changing economy. The programme must give workers and students usable skills rather than treat the availability of technology as sufficient preparation in itself.",
  "USA_1970_1996_rep_1_the_1997_budget_and_tax_settlement": "A budget and tax settlement must connect promised relief to the responsibilities the government retains. Its durability will depend on a coalition prepared to defend the resulting balance when individual provisions become politically costly.",
  "USA_1970_1996_rep_2_preparedness_without_nation_building": "Preparedness without nation-building seeks a force ready for defined security tasks and restrained in its wider commitments. Clear missions will matter if caution is to become a strategy rather than uncertainty presented as principle.",
  "USA_1970_1996_rep_3_internet_tax_freedom_act": "Internet tax policy will shape the conditions under which new commercial services develop. A lighter burden may support growth while limiting the revenue and discretion available to governments facing the costs of a changing market.",
  "USA_1970_1996_rep_4_information_age_force_modernization": "Information-age modernisation must connect sensors, communications and trained personnel. Better equipment will improve military capability only when doctrine and support allow services to use it together.",
  "USA_1970_1996_common_y2k_readiness_act": "The date change exposes dependencies hidden inside public and commercial information systems. Readiness requires testing, replacement and coordination before failures become a disruption that no single agency can repair alone.",
  "USA_1970_E0": "American industrial strength rests on regions and sectors facing very different pressures. The government must choose how public support, private investment and the demands of national defence should shape the next productive economy.",
  "USA_1970_E1": "Federal industrial grants can direct resources towards projects private finance will not undertake alone. Their terms must reward useful capacity and local opportunity rather than protect every enterprise able to obtain political support.",
  "USA_1970_E2": "Market investment zones will offer selected locations more attractive conditions for enterprise. The programme must translate incentives into productive activity instead of merely moving firms between competing public subsidies.",
  "USA_1970_E3": "Modernisation in the Great Plains can connect rural production to better equipment and services. Investment should strengthen the region's existing capabilities without assuming that every community can follow the same industrial model.",
  "USA_1970_E4": "Metropolitan offices can support a growing commercial and professional economy. Their expansion also places demands on infrastructure and local administration, making the relationship between development and public costs increasingly important.",
  "USA_1970_E5": "The interstate network needs renewal to remain a dependable foundation for commerce. Maintaining links between regions can make existing productive capacity more useful without relying entirely on the construction of new destinations.",
  "USA_1970_E6": "Defence procurement corridors connect suppliers, specialised skills and public orders. A coordinated programme can deepen military production while drawing resources towards industries whose demand depends heavily on federal decisions.",
  "USA_1970_E7": "Targeted growth programmes seek opportunities obscured by national averages. Public support must identify viable local strengths and a credible path beyond the period in which assistance makes investment easier.",
  "USA_1970_E8": "Looser metropolitan zoning can open more land and buildings to development. The benefits of a wider supply must be weighed against the public services and infrastructure needed by expanding urban communities.",
  "USA_1970_E9": "North American trade arrangements can connect producers across national markets. Negotiations must address access and adjustment together, with actual partner agreement establishing the obligations each government accepts.",
  "USA_1970_E10": "The information economy draws on research, communications and a workforce able to use new systems. Its development requires investment in those foundations rather than an assumption that technological promise will spread its benefits unaided.",
  "USA_1970_E11": "A post-industrial bargain must connect new opportunity to communities whose older sources of employment are changing. Skills and investment can help, but the government must acknowledge that the transition imposes real and uneven costs.",
  "USA_1970_N0": "America's energy position combines large domestic resources with exposure to external supply and changing demand. A national strategy must confront the costs of dependence without treating every alternative as immediately available.",
  "USA_1970_N1": "Conservation can reduce the energy needed to sustain ordinary economic activity. Better equipment and habits require investment and coordination, but can improve resilience without waiting for another major source of supply.",
  "USA_1970_N2": "Continental hydrocarbons offer a route towards stronger domestic supply. Development must connect access, extraction and transport while addressing the environmental and regulatory responsibilities attached to a larger programme.",
  "USA_1970_N3": "Standardisation can make nuclear construction and operation more consistent across projects. A common approach still needs technical competence and public confidence in the institutions responsible for safety and delivery.",
  "USA_1970_N4": "A strategic petroleum reserve gives the government a buffer against disrupted supply. Building and maintaining it requires resources now so that a future emergency need not be answered entirely through immediate scarcity.",
  "USA_1970_N5": "Renewable deployment corridors can connect suitable locations to equipment, investment and useful demand. Concentrating support will help emerging activity develop a practical base while leaving the government responsible for the programme's costs.",
  "USA_1970_N6": "Grid modernisation can make existing and new generation more dependable. Transmission, management and maintenance must work together if greater capacity is to become reliable power for households and industry.",
  "USA_1970_N7": "Continental pipelines connect production to consumers across long distances and political boundaries. Their value depends on viable routes, continuing operation and agreements that address the responsibilities of the jurisdictions involved.",
  "USA_1970_N8": "An energy-secure republic needs a combination of supply, conservation and resilient infrastructure. Bringing those programmes together can reduce vulnerability without promising that a large economy will ever be insulated from every external shock.",
  "USA_1970_F0": "American primacy creates demands that exceed any single department's view of national interests. The government must decide where leadership requires a commitment and where restraint preserves the resources needed elsewhere.",
  "USA_1970_F1": "Commercial diplomacy can widen access for American enterprise while strengthening political relationships. Its usefulness depends on agreements partners accept and firms can use, rather than treating every market as a reward for national influence.",
  "USA_1970_F2": "Rules-based leadership asks the United States to support institutions that can also constrain its choices. Reliable procedures may deepen cooperation, provided Washington accepts obligations alongside the authority it seeks to exercise.",
  "USA_1970_F3": "Interventionist leadership claims a greater willingness to use American power against threats abroad. That posture requires sustained military and political resources and a judgment about which objectives justify the burden.",
  "USA_1970_F4": "The Atlantic bargain depends on allies recognising both protection and reciprocal responsibility. Renewing it will require confidence in American commitments and a realistic account of what partners are prepared to contribute.",
  "USA_1970_F5": "Triangular diplomacy seeks room to manoeuvre through the relationships among major powers. Its success depends on actual channels and accepted terms rather than the assumption that one rival can always be used against another.",
  "USA_1970_F6": "The Middle Eastern balance connects regional security, external relationships and access to energy. A coherent policy must recognise the interests of local governments instead of assuming that American priorities alone determine their decisions.",
  "USA_1970_F7": "Security assistance to Israel can strengthen a close partner and America's influence over regional defence. Its terms must define practical cooperation while accounting for the effect that support has on wider diplomatic relationships.",
  "USA_1970_F8": "An honest broker must offer proposals the parties can judge on their substance. Credibility requires sustained engagement and a willingness to distinguish accepted commitments from a settlement Washington would merely prefer.",
  "USA_1970_F9": "An Arab trade and energy compact can connect commercial interests to a broader diplomatic relationship. Negotiated terms must give partners reasons to cooperate without presenting access to energy as an entitlement of American influence.",
  "USA_1970_F10": "A network of partnerships can distribute cooperation across several governments and institutions. Its strength will lie in commitments that participants actually honour rather than a growing list of relationships described as alliances.",
  "USA_1970_S0": "Civil rights and social change have left claims that legal declarations alone cannot settle. The government must decide how national standards, local institutions and public resources will make citizenship more equal in practice.",
  "USA_1970_S1": "Federal enforcement can make civil rights less dependent on the willingness of local authorities. Its expansion must provide the staff and legal capacity needed to protect rights when enforcement becomes politically contested.",
  "USA_1970_S2": "State-negotiated compliance seeks practical agreements with institutions responsible for delivery. Flexibility may ease resistance, but national commitments must remain more than promises whose meaning changes at every state border.",
  "USA_1970_S3": "Fair housing and equal credit affect where families can live and how they build economic security. Effective standards will require enforcement capable of reaching decisions often hidden within ordinary commercial practice.",
  "USA_1970_S4": "Making the Equal Rights Amendment a priority puts constitutional equality at the centre of the administration's political effort. Support must be organised through the institutions whose assent is required rather than assumed from executive endorsement.",
  "USA_1970_S5": "Tribal self-determination asks federal institutions to recognise a stronger indigenous role in governing local affairs. Resources and authority must be aligned if the policy is to mean more than transferring responsibility without the means to exercise it.",
  "USA_1970_S6": "Treatment before punishment would give health and recovery a larger place in drug policy. The government must build accessible services while deciding which enforcement responsibilities remain necessary alongside them.",
  "USA_1970_S7": "The national drug-policy debate concerns public health, enforcement and the social costs of both. A durable approach must choose priorities openly rather than promise that every agency can pursue its preferred solution without limits.",
  "USA_1970_S8": "A new civic compact must connect equal rights to institutions that citizens can use. Consolidating those responsibilities can give social reform a foundation stronger than a succession of separate legislative victories.",
  "USA_1970_D0": "Military reform must respond to operational experience and changing national expectations. The government needs a force whose personnel, institutions and methods can support the missions it is actually prepared to undertake.",
  "USA_1970_D1": "An all-volunteer force depends on recruitment, professional incentives and the retention of trained personnel. The change can strengthen the relationship between service and commitment while creating continuing demands on the defence budget.",
  "USA_1970_D2": "Renewed national service would retain a wider public obligation to provide manpower. Its legitimacy depends on fair administration and a clear account of why the country's requirements cannot be met on another basis.",
  "USA_1970_D3": "Intelligence under law requires effective collection and enforceable institutional limits. Clear authority and oversight can make the system more credible without denying that secrecy creates difficult questions of accountability.",
  "USA_1970_D4": "A freer covert hand gives intelligence agencies more discretion in pursuing opportunities abroad. The government must accept the political exposure and reduced oversight that accompany the additional reach it seeks.",
  "USA_1970_D5": "AirLand Battle requires land and air forces to plan and operate as parts of one campaign. Doctrine, communications and training must connect the capabilities each service has developed separately.",
  "USA_1970_D6": "A maritime strategy must connect naval strength to the political purposes of forward operations. Readiness and support are necessary if distant commitments are to remain credible beyond the first deployment.",
  "USA_1970_D7": "The Second Offset seeks an advantage through technology, precision and the integration of information. Research and procurement must be matched by training and doctrine able to turn advanced systems into usable military capability.",
  "USA_1970_D8": "Credible but constrained power requires forces that can fulfil clear commitments under accepted political limits. Bringing the reforms together will help the country preserve capability without treating military reach as a reason for unlimited obligation."
